title: Granger Causality in Expectiles: an M-vine copula test
hypothesis: H0: GC_tau(Z->X)=0 (no Granger causality in tau-expectile); H1: GC_tau>0; reject if p=(1/B) sum I(hat GC^{0}_{tau,j} >= hat GC_tau) < alpha
data_sources: Yahoo Finance daily prices SP500, FTSE100, Nikkei225, SSE Composite, Hang Seng Index Sept 2012-Oct 2014 transformed to log-returns *100; simulation DGPs as defined (Gaussian white noise, sstd nu=5 xi=-1.5 GARCH)
sample: Simulation: (X_t,Y_t,Z_t) k=1 Markov stationary. Size DGPs S1 (3 independent AR(1) 0.5 with N(0,1)) and S2 (3 independent GARCH(1,1) 0.01+0.08 e_{t-1}^2+0.87 sigma_{t-1}^2 with sstd(0,1,nu=5,xi=-1.5)). Power DGPs P1 (X_t=0.5 X_{t-1}+0.2 Y_{t-1}+0.2 Z_{t-1}+eta), P2 (X_t=0.5 X_{t-1}+5 Y_{t-1}Z_{t-1}+eta; Y,Z AR(1) 0.25), P3 (X_t=0.5 X_{t-1}+5 Y_{t-1}Z_{t-1}+eta; Y,Z N(0,1)), P4 (X_t=0.5 X_{t-1}+2.5 Y_{t-1}Z_{t-1}+epsilon; epsilon GARCH sstd as S2). Each cell aggregates S=500 Monte Carlo replications at T=100,200,500 and tau=0.1,0.5,0.9. Comparison P1: additional pairwise M-vine Y->X, Z->X and KNP quantile tests. Linear F-test: joint (Y,Z)->X mean. P3 appendix pairwise check at T=500, tau=1/2. Empirical Global: log-returns r_t=(log(s_t)-log(s_{t-1}))*100 of SP500, FTSE100, Nikkei225 daily Sept 2012-Oct 2014, T=500. Empirical Asian: log-returns of NK, HSI, SSE daily Sept 2012-Oct 2014, T=500. 9 directions x7 taus per application.
method: 1. Assume (X_t,Z_{1,t}..Z_{d,t}) strictly stationary k-Markov square-integrable with k=1, d=2 (d+1=3 series). Define tau-expectile mu_tau(X)=argmin_m E[R_tau(X-m)] with R_tau(X-m)=|tau-I{(X-m)<0}|(X-m)^2 = tau (X-m)_+^2+(1-tau)(X-m)_-^2. Define GC_tau(Z->X)=log( E[R_tau(X_t-mu_tau(X_t|I_X(t-k))) ] / E[R_tau(X_t-mu_tau(X_t|I_{X,Z}(t-k))) ] ). For tau=1/2 equals GC_mean.

2. Estimate hat GC_tau(Z->X)=log( sum_{t=T0}^{T} R_tau(x_t-hat mu_tau(X_t|X_{t-1}=x_{t-1})) / sum_{t=T0}^{T} R_tau(x_t-hat mu_tau(X_t|X_{t-1}=x_{t-1},Z_{t-1}=z_{t-1})) ) with T0=T/2. hat mu_tau computed via M-vine.

3. Step A1: fit M-vine copula to M_x=(x_t)_{t=1..T} via selection/estimation of nagler2022 for stationary vines. Step A2: for each t=T0..T generate N=200 iid predictions tilde x^{M_x}_{i,t} of X_t|X_{t-1}=x_{t-1} from fitted vine, compute hat mu_{tau,N}=argmin_m sum_{i=1}^N R_tau(tilde x^{M_x}_{i,t}-m). Step A3: repeat A1-A2 on M_{x,vz}=(x_t,vz_t) to obtain hat mu_{tau,N}(X_t|X_{t-1}=x_{t-1},Z_{t-1}=vz_{t-1}).

4. Test H0: GC_tau=0 vs H1:hat GC_tau>0. Part B p-value via vine bootstrap under H0 preserving dependence: B1 extract c_{X_t,X_{t+1}} and c_{X_t,Z_{1,t}} from Tree1 of M_{x,vz} vine; B2 generate x_t^0~hat F_X then x_{t+1}^0|c_{X_t,X_{t+1}}; B3 generate z_{1,t}^0|c_{X_t,Z_{1,t}} using hat F_{Z1}; B4 for i=2..d extract c_{X_t,Z_{i,t};Z_{1..i-1}} from Tree i and draw z_{i,t}^0| x_t^0,z_{1..i-1,t}^0 using hat F_{Zi}; B5 compute hat GC^{0}_{tau,j} on simulated {(x_t^0,vz_t^0)}_{t=1..T}; B6 repeat B=200 times; B7 p=(1/B) sum_j I(hat GC^{0}_{tau,j} >= hat GC_tau). Reject if p<alpha with alpha=0.05.

5. Simulation evaluates empirical size (S1,S2) and power (P1-P4) as rejection rates over S=500 replications at each tau in {0.1,0.5,0.9} and T in {100,200,500} with N=200,B=200,T0=T/2. Linear F-test comparison uses restricted/unrestricted AR for (Y,Z)->X mean. Pairwise P3 check uses pairwise M-vine tau=1/2 and linear F at alpha=0.05,S=500,T=500.
6. Empirical applies same specification N=200,B=200,T0=T/2 to log-returns r_t*100 at tau in {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9,0.95} for 6 pairwise +3 joint directions per application, each on T=500.
